name: Marie Curie
role: Scientist, Discoverer & Quiet Fighter of the Dark
famous_quote: Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood.
character_sheet: Marie as a 10-year-old girl with braided dark blonde hair, grey eyes, a simple charcoal wool dress with a white collar.
cover_scene: Marie as a 10-year-old girl with braided dark blonde hair, grey eyes, a simple charcoal wool dress with a white collar, holding a glowing glass tube in a dim laboratory, her face lit by a soft blue-green light.
story_childhood:
In a busy city called Warsaw,
a baby girl was born.

Her name was Maria.
Everyone called her Manya.

She loved to read.
She read everything she found.

Her father taught science.
He kept shiny tools on a shelf.

Manya stared at them for hours.
She wanted to know how things worked.
childhood_scene: A wide view of old Warsaw at dusk, rooftops and church spires under a grey Polish sky, cobbled streets, horse carts, and lamplight glowing in tall narrow windows.
story_takeaway: Keep working, one small step at a time, and the dark will give up its secrets.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Loved to Learn
chapters.narrative:
Manya was very clever.
She won prizes at school.

But girls could not go
to university back then.

That did not stop her.
She studied in secret classes.

She saved every coin.
She dreamed of far-off Paris.

She worked as a teacher
to help her sister first.

Her turn would come.
She was sure of it.
chapters.scene: Marie as a 10-year-old girl with braided dark blonde hair, grey eyes, a simple charcoal wool dress with a white collar, reading a heavy book by candlelight at a wooden desk piled with papers.

chapters.title: Paris and Pale Blue Light
chapters.narrative:
At last she reached Paris.
She changed her name to Marie.

She was often cold and hungry.
She ate only bread and tea.

But she loved her studies.
Numbers and metals filled her days.

She met a kind man, Pierre.
He loved science too.

Together they wondered
about strange, glowing rocks.

What made them shine?
chapters.scene: A grown Marie with dark blonde hair pinned up and grey eyes, in a plain dark dress, standing beside Pierre in a cluttered Paris attic laboratory with glass beakers and a small iron stove.

chapters.title: The Cold, Leaky Shed
chapters.narrative:
They worked in an old shed.
Rain dripped through the roof.

Marie stirred huge boiling pots.
Her arms ached every night.

She boiled tons of rock
to find a tiny speck.

Many said she would fail.
Marie did not listen.

For four long years
she stirred and waited.

At last, in the dark,
something glowed.
chapters.scene: A grown Marie with dark blonde hair and grey eyes, in a stained apron, stirring an enormous steaming cauldron in a shabby wooden shed, rain leaking from the roof, glass jars around her.

chapters.title: A Light in the Darkness
chapters.narrative:
She had found it.
A new element, glowing blue.

She named one radium,
for its magic light.

The world was amazed.
She won the greatest prize.

Then she won it again.
No woman had ever done that.

Her discovery would one day
help doctors heal the sick.

All from years
of never giving up.
chapters.scene: A grown Marie with dark blonde hair and grey eyes cupping a small glass vial of glowing blue-green light in a darkened laboratory, her tired face full of quiet awe, glassware glinting around her.

modern.title: If Marie Were 10 Today
modern.narrative:
If Marie were ten today,
she would love the library.

She would ask endless questions
in her science class.

She might code little robots.
She might study glowing stars.

When something seemed too hard,
she would try once more.

She would tell shy girls
that their ideas matter too.

The world would be her lab.
modern.scene: Marie as a 10-year-old girl with braided dark blonde hair, grey eyes, a simple charcoal wool dress with a white collar, peering through a microscope in a bright modern classroom with a laptop and colorful science posters.

timeline.caption: Maria is born in Warsaw, Poland.
timeline.scene: A modest Warsaw townhouse with a lamp glowing in the window on a snowy November evening, no people present.

timeline.caption: She moves to Paris to study science.
timeline.scene: A steam train arriving at a busy Paris station, a single traveler's trunk resting on the platform.

timeline.caption: Marie and Pierre discover radium and polonium.
timeline.scene: A tiny glass dish holding a faint blue-glowing speck on a laboratory bench in a dim shed at night.

timeline.caption: She wins her first Nobel Prize in Physics.
timeline.scene: A golden Nobel medal resting on a velvet cushion beside a rolled certificate, warm light around them.

timeline.caption: She wins a second Nobel Prize, in Chemistry.
timeline.scene: Two Nobel medals side by side on a wooden desk cluttered with glass vials and handwritten notes.

after_treasures.title: Gifts That Live On
after_treasures.narrative:
Marie gave the world
more than shining metals.

She gave us new ideas.
She gave us courage.

Her work helps doctors
find and fight disease.

Her name still means
never, ever give up.

Each gift below
came from her patient hands.

All from a girl
who loved to learn.
after_treasures.scene: A quiet laboratory bench at dawn, sunlight touching glass tubes, notebooks, and a faintly glowing vial, no people present.

lessons.lesson: Keep going even when the work is slow and hard.
Ask how things work, then go and find out.
Do brave things even when others doubt you.
Share what you learn to help other people.
